<a id="welcome-to-slackblocks"></a>
# Welcome to `slackblocks`!

<p align="center">
  <img width="30%" src="/slackblocks/img/legacy/e571b02afbd2c2af10a05d1d4cf23ef23b939f92/sb.png" />
</p>

`slackblocks` is Python package for creating complex Slack messages 
    using the Slack [BlockKit API](https://api.slack.com/block-kit).

It exists so you don't have to define block-based Slack messages by
    hand-writing JSON.

## Components {#components}

The [Slack BlockKit API](https://api.slack.com/block-kit) defines a number of 
    different resource types (all defined in JSON) which work together to 
    define Block-based messages.

`slackblocks` makes using this API easier by providing a hierarchy of Python
    classes that represent these resources.

### Objects {#objects}
[`Objects`](/v1.0.0/reference/objects) (e.g. [`Text`](/v1.0.0/reference/objects#objects.Text)) 
    are the lowest level pimitives that are used to populate 
    [`Elements`](/v1.0.0/reference/elements) and [`Blocks`](/v1.0.0/reference/blocks).

### Elements {#elements}
[`Elements`](/v1.0.0/reference/elements) are typically interactive UI elements that take
    in [`Object`](/v1.0.0/reference/objects) to define their content. For example, the 
    [`CheckboxGroup`](/v1.0.0/reference/elements/#elements.CheckboxGroup) element takes in one or
    more [`Option`](/v1.0.0/reference/objects#objects.Option) items and presents a
    checkbox menu to the user with those options.

### Blocks {#blocks}
[`Blocks`](/v1.0.0/reference/blocks) are the core element of the API, with different 
    [`Blocks`](/v1.0.0/reference/blocks) used to create different types of visual
    elements. For example, the [`DividerBlock`](/v1.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.DividerBlock), 
    when rendered, will show a visual element similar to a `<hr>` HTML element. The
    [`RichTextBlock`](/v1.0.0/reference/blocks#blocks.RichTextBlock) on the other hand
    allows for the display of text elements with visual styling like italics,
    block quotes, lists and code blocks. 

### Messages {#messages}
[`Messages`](/v1.0.0/reference/messages) are a convenience wrapper around `Blocks` that
    can be unpacked as arguments straight into the official Slack Python SDK (or
    its legacy `slackclient` counterpart).

### Views {#views}
[`Views`](/v1.0.0/reference/views/) are an alternative usage for [`Blocks`](/v1.0.0/reference/blocks)
    that allow for the creation of custom UI "surfaces" within Slack, e.g. for 
    third-party apps.
